decisions.q: How to count dimensions an L2 fit uses
decisions.rule: The fewest dimensions holding 90% of absolute coefficient mass (dimensions_holding_share, MASS_SHARE). The non-zero count is reported beside it and never compared across encoders, because L2 zeroes nothing.

decisions.q: Paired retrieval-minus-classifier contrasts outside the primary encoder
decisions.rule: None. The other three encoders' per-patient classifier test predictions are not on disk, so their retrieval is reported at each metric's best k without a paired contrast.

decisions.q: How retrieval is framed in the paper
decisions.rule: Nearest and random neighbours, each swept over every k from 1 to 34,063; no single k is the headline. ROC curves and confusion matrices only at each arm's best k. No farthest-neighbour retrieval in any document.
Main text, on the owner's answer: manuscript Figure 6, in Nearest-Neighbor Retrieval Across Encoders. Its dimension counts describe fitted models and carry no sampling interval.

decisions.q: Best-k ROC curves and confusion matrices: all four encoders or the primary only
decisions.rule: All four, on the owner's answer: supplement S6, Figures S8-S9. A-C are the primary's 3 arms, D-I each other encoder's 2 nearest-neighbour metrics. Random does not use the embedding, so it is drawn once.
Figure 5 is a Figure-4-style panel per non-primary encoder, each that encoder's neighbor_count_sweep_manuscript.png. Figure 4 is the primary's and is not repeated. The bandless overlay is out.

threads.title: The estimand and its identification
threads.question: Which antidepressant class at the index anchor carries the lower predicted TRD risk for this patient, and under what assumptions is that comparison causal?

tasks.text: Learn: the target trial at the index anchor, its treatment, eligibility, time zero and outcome
Learn: gradeable against ungradeable predictions, and why the arm actually received is the only performance evidence
Learn: conditional independence, and why confounding by indication survives adjustment for measured covariates
Learn: why the 0.10/0.90 trim changes the estimand to the overlap population
Learn: the four-rung robustness ladder, and what each rung can and cannot rule out

decisions.rule: Index anchor: the class at the anchor prescription, pairwise over snri_vs_ssri, bupropion_vs_ssri and bupropion_vs_snri. The TRD label is the outcome, feature vectors only, Paper 1's split reused. The switch-decision framing is deferred.
Comparison-arm-first: effect is risk(comparison) minus risk(reference), so a positive effect means the first-named arm raises P(TRD).

threads.title: The T-learner counterfactual pipeline
threads.question: Per contrast: two arm models, a propensity model, the trimmed and overlap-weighted averages with refit-inside-the-bootstrap intervals, population accounting and the CV layer.

tasks.text: Build: pull the per-arm calibration bin table out of grade_arm_models into its own function, and have run_one.py persist it per arm
Build: one folder per contrast carrying the SMD table, the E-value and its benchmark table, and the negative-control result beside what is there now

decisions.q: Which bootstrap interval the paper reports
decisions.rule: Both, separately: estimation resamples training rows with the test frame fixed, and total resamples both. The paper names the one it quotes.
The frozen 80/20 split stays the headline and keeps the interval. Five folds sit beside it, reported as fold mean and between-fold spread, never fused with the interval.

decisions.q: A train-side panel on the propensity figure
The symmetric 0.10/0.90 band, or a rule that adapts to arm prevalence
Whether population_report carries a per-fold section

threads.title: Rung 1: covariate balance (SMD)
threads.question: After the trim and the overlap weights, are the two arms balanced on every measured covariate?

tasks.text: Coach: the owner writes the SMD per covariate from balance_frame.csv, as mean difference over pooled SD
Coach: the owner decides how a multi-level categorical field becomes balance rows
Build: the Love plot over the three balance tables

decisions.rule: Three: raw over every eligible test row, hard-trimmed over the in-band rows, and overlap-weighted as a sensitivity column. The comfort threshold is |SMD| under 0.1.

decisions.q: Further balance measures (variance ratios, a distributional distance)

threads.title: Rung 2: overlap and positivity
threads.question: Is the propensity model fit to judge overlap, and how much do the two arm-conditional propensity densities share?

tasks.text: Coach: the owner writes the overlap coefficient, the integrated minimum of the two arm-conditional e(x) densities

decisions.rule: The hard-trimmed average over the 0.10/0.90 band is the headline. The overlap-weighted average, e(x)(1 - e(x)), is the sensitivity. Trimmed and retained counts are reported per arm.

threads.title: Rung 3: the E-value
threads.question: How strong would an unmeasured confounder have to be to explain each contrast away, against the strongest measured covariate?

tasks.text: Coach: the owner writes the E-value on the point estimate and on the CI limit nearest the null
Coach: the owner writes both risk-ratio arrows for every measured covariate, the benchmark the E-value is read against

threads.title: Rung 4: a negative-control outcome
threads.question: Does the identical pipeline find an effect on an outcome the drug class cannot plausibly cause? A non-zero one indicts the design.

tasks.text: Coach: the owner chooses the negative-control outcome and argues why it qualifies
Build: extract that outcome's label from the raw diagnosis tables, as a second binary label the pipeline can re-run against

threads.title: The causal forest, Paper 2's triangulating estimator
threads.question: Does CausalForestDML, under selection on observables, agree with the T-learner on each contrast?

decisions.rule: Paper 2, as the triangulating estimator against the T-learner. Paper 1 names it as future work only, unless a reviewer asks.

decisions.q: How a positive average effect is read
decisions.rule: As residual confounding by indication until the falsification battery says otherwise. Any BLP hit is hypothesis-generating.
